question.problem:
| **Age, in years ($x$)** | $10$ | $11$ | $12$ | $15$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Weight, in kg ($y$)** | $30$ | $40$ | $40$ | $50$ |

The table above shows the ages and corresponding weights of four students. Compute the covariance of the data sets.
question.worked_solution:
The (population) covariance of the data sets $x=\{{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}\}$ and $y=\{{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}\}$ is given by 

$$
\text{Cov}(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

First, we need to compute the means:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (10+11+12+15) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 48 \\  & =12 \\ \overset{―}{y} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (30+40+40+50) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 160 \\  & =40\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(10\,-\,12)(30\,-\,40)+(11\,-\,12)(40\,-\,40)+(12\,-\,12)(40\,-\,40)+(15\,-\,12)(50\,-\,40)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(-2)(-10)+(-1)(0)+(0)(0)+(3)(10)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[20+0+0+30] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 50 \\  & =12.5.\end{aligned}
$$
